basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 18.' and it opens 'VERS. 18.-- Dixit quoque Deus: Non est bonum esse hominem solum. Faciamus ei adjutorem'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 18.-- Dixit quoque Deus: Non est bonum esse hominem solum. Faciamus ei adjutorem similem sui. Hic enim ostenditur quia uxor propter solatium et adjutorium creata est viro, et ideo solatium ei praebere debet atque subdita esse [ Z., ideo ut solatium ei praeberet, atque subdita esset], teste Apostolo: Mulier sui corporis potestatem non habet [Z., habeat ], sed vir. Sed requirendum videtur quare Adam mundi dominus legem acceperit. Ideo, ne se extolleret dominio, sed in observatione mandati sciret se subjectum esse Conditori.
